scores.rationale: The proposed default preserves employment and limits weekly commitment, partially expressing work compatibility. It does not explicitly prioritize a flexible or modular learning path.
No sources or evidence classes are identified for evaluating program flexibility or compatibility with work and family.
No named learning option is supported by a verifiable flexibility-related fact.
The report asks about full-time study but supplies no concrete fact about a named option or route's disruptive requirements.
No substantive comparison identifies a consequential difference between flexible learning and full-time study.
No learning option is recommended because it supports work-compatible flexibility.
No option is downgraded because of full-time study or its disruption.
The report contains no executable learning or experimentation step implementing a flexible path.

The default scenario supplies a concrete weekly time allowance compatible with continued employment. However, it remains a proposed planning assumption rather than an allocation or rule within an actual plan.
Asking whether a career break is possible does not state a condition under which full-time study becomes the better choice.
No evidence about a learning option is linked to the flexibility preference and a downstream decision or action.
